ledger.note: 13-24 May 1867: Kansala falls to Futa Jallon and its Fula allies: "Victory of Futa Jallon".

region.text: Kaabu's heartland round Kansala, destroyed in May 1867

ledger.note: 1867: Kaabu's heartland passes under Fula control. "Kansala stayed under Fula control until the Portuguese suppression around 1900."

1867: Imamate control is extended into Fuladu. "In 1867, the Battle of Kansala destroyed Kaabu's capital, extending Imamate control into Fuladu." The Kaabu page says Fuladu "gained its independence" under Alpha Molo Balde.

1896: the relation with Fuladu ends with the imamate's sovereignty. No page dates the end of Fuladu's dependence; around 1900 the Portuguese, British and French absorbed the remaining kingdoms (Kaabu page).

wars.outcome: A French treaty of 1881 believed to create a protectorate (the Arabic text had no such clauses); a 1893 treaty validated the Fula reading; Bokar Biro was beaten at Bantignel on 13 December 1895, restored with French help in early 1896, then deposed on 3 November and killed at Porédaka on 14 November 1896.

notes:
Imamate of Futa Jallon (the Emirate of Timbo), additions batch af-03-x; Cliopatria has no row. Pages: Imamate of Futa Jallon, Fouta Djallon (thin), Kaabu, Battle of Kansala.

End: the infobox says disestablished 1912 (last sovereign Boubacar IV, 1906-1912) but the French deposed Bokar Biro and entered Timbo in November 1896 (protectorate from 18 November 1896); this dossier ends in 1896/11 and the french-africa dossier should carry the 1896-1912 protectorate as a vassal_start. The Imamate page's succession disputes (1791, alternation Soriya and Alfaya every two years from 1845) have no land effect. The page names no vassal states other than the Kaabu war; Solimana, Kouranko, Kissi etc. are not on it. Samory (1879 alliance) is a Wassoulou note. Fouta Djallon also says the highlands were a province of Sosso and Mali as Dialonkadugu.

Needs dossiers: fuladu (Alfa Molo, 1867-c.1900), kaabu (written here), the Futa Jallon provinces (nine) are not named on the pages. Gazetteer: Timbo, Talansan, Poredaka, Bantignel (places).
